messages:
geeta: idea: run a small experiment to reduce stale postmortem actions. call it 'closure duty roster' — single tracker + weekly 15m sync + short escalation ladder. keep it lightweight so people actually use it.

omar: sounds good. what's the escalation ladder part?

geeta: short: owner -> closure_owner -> oncall -> eng-lead. closure_owner is a rotating role who nudges owners, verifies fixes, and closes items when verification passes. not the same as the remediation owner.

vik: can we have an automated 'age' flag on items >30d and a weekly CSV of repeat signatures? that'll help prioritization.

oncall-bot: Notice: INC-2417 has 1 follow-up >30d. Please assign closure_owner.

geeta: draft tracker cols below (super compact):
```
incident_id, short_summary, remediation_owner, closure_owner, next_action, due_date(YYYY-MM-DD), status, verification_checks, recurrence_count, rca_link
```

omar: add a tiny 'regression_gate' entry under verification_checks: metric + check @7d and @30d. helps avoid ship-and-forget.

rachel: i'll spin up the tracker as a Google Sheet and add a calendar invite for a Wednesday 09:00 PT 15m slot. will default closure_owner = oncall that week, can reassign.

vik: i'll prototype a recurrence detector (hash(error_text + top_stackframe)) and output top recurrent issues weekly. target prototype in 5 days.

ageed: (typo)

geeta: immediate action items:
- create tracker + invite (rachel) - due 2111111130
- recurrence prototype (vik) - due 2111111550
- migrate backlog >30d into tracker and assign closure_owner (omar) - due 2111111200
- update oncall SOP with duty roster + escalation ladder (geeta) - due 2111111300

omar: i'll start migration and ping owners for missing fields. keeping columns minimal will help adoption. :+1:

rachel: invite created and sheet live. sharing now.

oncall-bot: Reminder set: weekly closure-duty sync every Wed 09:00 PT.

geeta: thanks all. we'll run the pilot 6 weeks, measure closure-rate, median days-to-close, and recurrence hits. if it improves things, fold into the standard oncall playbook. :rocket:
